newsitem.title: FRANCE: France sets price on sale of more Bull shares.
newsitem.headline: France sets price on sale of more Bull shares.

text.p: The French finance ministry said it was selling from Wednesday a further 16.2 million shares in computer maker Bull, with institutional investors being offered stock at 38 francs ($6.61) per share.

News that the stake reduction was going ahead came after an earlier announcement on Tuesday that the sell-off of France Telecom was being postponed by a month to avoid clashing with an early parliamentary election called on Monday by President Jacques Chirac.

The ministry said in a statement it will sell a total 16.2 million shares in Cie des Machines Bull, fewer than the 18 million it said on April 11 it expected to dispose of. It would thereby cut its stake to 17 percent from 30.5 percent.
The government is selling the extra Bull shares to personal and institutional investors, with the latter getting 14.58 million shares at a price of 38 francs per share.
Some 1.62 million shares will be sold to private investors at 36 francs per share, with the stock being offered from Wednesday morning until the evening of April 28.

There is a 10 percent clawback on the institutional tranche in favour of retail investors if there is enough demand. The sale to institutions will be done through a book-building exercise and can be closed at any time from Wednesday.
The government has given banks handling the institutional sale an option to buy a further 900,000 shares.

Some 1.8 million shares have been set aside for Bull employees and former staff, with a possible further 100,000 shares available if the selling banks in the institutional tranche exercise their option to buy more stock.
France Telecom holds an 18.7 percent stake in Bull, as do NEC Corp of Japan and Motorola Inc.
